children: BENCHMARK TREASURY YIELD BREAKS TO NEW HIGHS, BUT THE MOVE IS LOOKING STRETCHED
Long-dated Treasury yields continue to climb as the bond selloff shows few signs of easing.

The 30-year Treasury yield rose above 5.44% on Thursday, its highest level since 2004, while the benchmark 10-year yield climbed to 5.1497%, its highest level since 2007, before easing back to around 5.11%.

The latest leg higher follows Wednesday's stronger-than-expected economic data, reinforcing the view that resilient growth and sticky inflation remain a challenge for policymakers. In response, traders ramped up bets that the Federal Reserve may need to keep rates higher for longer, sending yields sharply higher across the curve.
From a technical standpoint, the 10-year yield is entering noteworthy territory.

It has pushed above its upper yearly Bollinger Band, currently near 5.11%, while also testing resistance at the 1993 low of 5.1514%. A sustained break above that level would mark another important waypoint in the multiyear advance in yields and shift the focus toward higher long-term targets.

However, the move is beginning to look stretched. Sustained trading outside the yearly Bollinger Bands is uncommon and typically requires truly runaway momentum, as was the case in the late 1970s and early 1980s.

Momentum indicators are flashing warning signs. The 9-year RSI has climbed to its highest reading since 1983, while weekly and monthly RSI readings are at their most overbought levels since October 2023. If yields begin to roll over, a bearish divergence could emerge on the daily chart.
None of this guarantees a pullback, but it suggests the advance may be becoming harder to sustain.

On the downside, initial support sits in the 5.04%-5.02% zone. A break below 4.92% would strengthen the case for a deeper retreat, while the rising 20-week moving average near 4.65% remains an important line in the sand. The 10-year yield has not posted a weekly close below that measure since late February.

If 5.1514% gives way, the next upside targets come into view near the 2007 high around 5.33%, followed by the 50-year moving average near 5.65%. Beyond that lies the 38.2% retracement of the 1981-2020 decline at 6.24%.
